The test image shows a tomato plant with a bleached/dried stem at the center, significant wilting and brown dead foliage throughout, and what appears to be stem girdling. The affected parts are the **stem** and **whole plant collapse**.

Top candidates: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (bleached stem, collapse), Southern_Blight (stem base wilting), Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers (dark stem cankers).

Let me view one reference per candidate.

Sclerotinia reference shows fluffy white mycelium + black sclerotia. Southern Blight reference shows bleached/whitish girdled stem. The test image has a bleached dried stem with total plant collapse — Southern Blight is looking like a strong match. Let me use my 4th view on Southern Blight whole plant.

**Analysis summary:**

- Test image: bleached/whitened dried stem at soil level, entire plant collapsed with brown dead foliage, black plastic mulch visible (commercial setting), wire trellis supports
- Sclerotinia reference: white fluffy mycelium + developing black sclerotia — no visible white fluff in test image
- Southern Blight stem reference (1575059): bleached/girdled stem at soil line — very similar to test image stem appearance
- Southern Blight whole plant reference (1575058): complete plant death/brown dried foliage — matches overall test scene well

The bleached, dried-out stem at the soil line with total plant collapse and dead brown foliage, combined with black plastic mulch (typical commercial tomato), aligns most closely with Southern Blight's characteristic soil-line girdling. Sclerotinia remains possible but usually shows more obvious white mycelium on the stem exterior.
